Crosstalk regulation involving tryptophan metabolites under biotic stress

Crosstalk regulation involving tryptophan metabolites under biotic stress.(A) The crosstalk between tryptophan metabolites regulates resistance to biotic stress. Under biotic stress, the crosstalk among auxin, melatonin, and IGs enhance plant defenses against pathogens, repel insects, and reduce susceptibility by regulating proteins such as TIR1 and PIN1/2, which are involved in auxin homeostasis and transport. Transcription factors MYB34, MYB51, MYB122, and WRKY33 modulate the metabolic flux of the IAOx pathway, facilitating the production of defense compounds including IGs, camalexin, and 4-OH-ICN. WRKY24 regulates the balance between melatonin and auxin during biotic stress. Additionally, melatonin directs sulfur and nitrogen metabolism into IG biosynthetic pathways, promoting IG production.(B) The crosstalk between tryptophan metabolites and other phytohormones regulates resistance to biotic stress. Auxin, regulated by phytohormones such as SA and JA, balances growth and defense through mediation of auxin homeostasis and signaling components, including GH3.5. Melatonin, induced by NO and ROS, activates plant immunity via the OXI1/MAPKKK3-MKK4/5/7/9-MPK3/6 cascade, stimulating SA to enhance resistance to biotic stress. Melatonin also induces JA and ET pathways to activate pathogen-resistance proteins. Furthermore, IG and camalexin production, stimulated by SA, JA, and ET, reinforces plant defenses. Melatonin increases MeJA levels, which elevate the signaling molecule H2S and induce defense-related enzymes such as TI, CI, PPO, and PAL. Additionally, S-nitrosylation of the melatonin synthase COMT2 and sulfenylation of the auxin synthase TSB1 contribute to balancing plant growth and defense responses.
